# Study overview {#sec-study-overview}

The **Norwegian COVID-19 Cohort (NCC / Koronastudien)** is a cohort study that
follows participants over time using self-reported questionnaires, linked
national health-registry records, and biological samples. This page is the
entry point to the study manual: it describes what the study is, how it is
designed, and who is in it. For the mechanics of how each type of data is
gathered and reaches the secure processing environment, see
@sec-data-collection.

## Study design

The study is a cohort followed **prospectively** through repeated
self-completed questionnaires, with participant-reported data extended by
**passive follow-up** through national registry linkage.

Data collection is organised into questionnaire *families*, each identified by
a single-letter prefix that is carried through to every variable derived from
it:

| Family | Role in the design |
|--------|--------------------|
| **B** (B1, B2) | Baseline — background characteristics at study entry |
| **F** (F1–F6, F7+ planned) | Repeated follow-up over the course of the study |
| **R** (R1–R6) | CLOC sub-study report questionnaires |
| **E** (E1–E3) | Supplementary instruments (incl. BRIEF, RAND-12, ISARIC) |
| **Q** (Q1) | Short quick-response questionnaire |

A participant answers a given questionnaire at most once, so each form yields
one row per participant. Registry data, which is longitudinal by nature, is
summarised to the same one-row-per-participant shape before delivery. The
result is that every source in the study is joinable `1:1` on `deltaker_id` —
the property that the whole data model rests on. See
[Data management](../best-practices/data-management.qmd) for what this means in
practice.

Consent is maintained as a **separate datastream** from the questionnaire
responses, and withdrawals are re-applied on every processing run, so analyses
always reflect the current consent state rather than consent at the time of
response.

## Data sources

The study draws on three data channels, linked on `deltaker_id`:

1. **Questionnaires** — self-reported data collected through Nettskjema, the
   University of Oslo's survey platform, and transferred into TSD
   automatically.
2. **National health registries** — for consenting participants, under the
   study's approvals. Registries contribute objective, longitudinal health
   information that continues independently of whether a participant answers a
   questionnaire.
3. **Biological samples** — biobank material and derived laboratory results,
   including serology from dried blood spots.

| Registry | Contributes |
|----------|-------------|
| **MSIS** | Notifiable infectious-disease diagnoses (incl. SARS-CoV-2) |
| **SYSVAK** | Vaccinations (incl. COVID-19 doses) |
| **DÅR** | Cause-of-death records |
| **NPR** | Hospital and specialist-care contacts |
| **LMR** | Dispensed prescription medications |

Each source, and the route it takes into TSD, is documented in full in
@sec-data-collection. Some registry deliveries carry handling conditions that
are stricter than the study's general rules; those conditions are enforced in
processing and are described there.

## Sub-studies

Parts of the cohort take part in sub-studies that use their own questionnaires
and are delivered as their own topic datasets.

- **CLOC** — uses the R-family report questionnaires (R1–R6) and is delivered
  as `cloc_dataset`.

## Governance and approvals

All person-level study data is stored and processed exclusively within **TSD**,
under tiered access controls that separate researcher-accessible data from the
most sensitive administrative data. Only aggregated results are brought out of
TSD — never person-level data. The tiers, and how to request access to
restricted fields, are described in
[Data management](../best-practices/data-management.qmd).

::: {.callout-important}
Approval documents, data processing agreements, and any material containing
identifiers must **not** be reproduced on this site — it is public. Link to the
secure internal location instead.
:::
